battle.name: 繼續戰爭
battle.theater: 卡累利阿地峽與拉多加湖畔
battle.brief: 1941年6月，芬蘭在德國支持下對蘇聯發動「繼續戰爭」，在卡累利阿地峽及拉多加湖畔展開激烈戰鬥，蘇聯以T-34坦克為主力突破防線，雙方陷入持久消耗。在漫長的冬季裡，T-34的裝甲與火力令芬蘭防線多次被突破，雙方陷入激烈消耗。

kit.name: T-34坦克
kit.history: T-34是蘇聯在二戰中期部署的主力中型坦克，以傾斜裝甲與76公厘炮提升生存性與火力，成為蘇軍突破防線的骨幹。

countries: 芬蘭與蘇聯是1941年繼續戰爭的主要交戰國。芬蘭在1941年6月25日正式向蘇聯宣戰，動員了包括第1、第2、第3兵團在內的十餘萬正規軍，並在德國的物資援助下組建了獨立的空軍與海軍力量。蘇聯則在卡累利阿前線部署了第23、第7軍團及多個步兵師，總兵力約二十萬人，並在列寧格勒軍區提供砲兵與坦克支援。雙方的後勤線路主要沿著拉多加湖西岸與芬蘭灣展開，德國的援助船隻通過波的尼亞灣向芬蘭港口輸送彈藥與燃料。這場戰役的範圍不僅覆蓋了卡累利阿地峽，還延伸至波的尼亞灣的海上交戰。
countriesEn: Finland and the Soviet Union were the principal belligerents of the Continuation War in 1941. Finland declared war on the Soviet Union on 25 June 1941, mobilizing more than one hundred thousand regular troops, including the I, II and III Corps, and, with German material assistance, established its own air force and navy. The Soviet Union deployed the 23rd and 7th Armies along the Karelian front, comprising several infantry divisions with a total strength of about two hundred thousand men, and provided artillery and tank support from the Leningrad Military District. The logistical routes of both sides ran primarily along the western shore of Lake Ladoga and the Gulf of Finland, with German supply ships delivering ammunition and fuel through the Gulf of Bothnia to Finnish ports. The scope of the campaign covered not only the Karelian Isthmus but also extended to naval engagements in the Gulf of Bothnia.
people: 芬蘭軍隊的核心指揮官是元帥卡爾·古斯特·埃米爾·曼納海姆，他在1941年7月10日親自督導第1兵團向維堡發起總攻。第1兵團師長阿爾托·哈爾塔率領的第4步兵師與第5步兵師在砲兵掩護下快速突破蘇軍第23軍團的左翼。第2兵團的師長尤霍·科普萊甯負責保護側翼，並調動輕裝甲車隊執行側翼掃蕩。蘇聯方面，第23軍團司令伊万·科瓦廖夫中將在防線重組上表現頑強，但在7月31日維堡陷落後被迫撤退。第7軍團的師長瓦西里·叶戈罗夫率部在拉多加湖東岸進行游擊抵抗，雖未能扭轉局面，但仍牽制了芬蘭部分兵力。這些高級軍官與基層指揮官共同塑造了戰役的節奏與走向。
peopleEn: The core of the Finnish command was Marshal Carl Gustaf Emil Mannerheim, who personally oversaw the I Corps' offensive toward Viipuri on 10 July 1941. The commander of the I Corps, Major General Aalto Halla, led the 4th and 5th Infantry Divisions, which, under artillery cover, swiftly broke through the left flank of the Soviet 23rd Army. The II Corps' commander, Major General Juhho Koplein, protected the flank and deployed light armoured vehicles to conduct sweeping operations. On the Soviet side, Lieutenant General Ivan Kovalev, commander of the 23rd Army, stubbornly reorganised his defences, but after the fall of Viipuri on 31 July he was forced to retreat. The 7th Army's commander, Major General Vasily Yegorov, led guerrilla resistance on the eastern bank of Lake Ladoga, and although unable to reverse the situation, he tied down considerable Finnish forces. These senior officers together with their junior commanders shaped the rhythm and direction of the campaign.
kits: 芬蘭軍隊的武器裝備在1941年已逐步現代化，步兵主要配備Suomi KP/31衝鋒槍、7.62mm口徑的Sissi M/44卡賓槍以及Vickers .303機槍。火力支援方面，裝甲師裝備了俘獲的蘇聯T-26與T-28坦克，並在必要時以Lahti L-39 37mm反坦克炮進行定點摧毀。砲兵則使用152mm 1910/30榴彈炮與120mm 1938型迫擊砲，每門砲每日消耗約150發高爆彈。蘇聯紅軍的步兵師標配莫辛-納甘步槍與DP-27輕機槍，並配備45mm 53-K反坦克炮與122mm 1938型榴彈炮。後勤方面，雙方均使用卡車與馬車混合運輸，芬蘭的後勤基地在圖爾庫和波的尼亞灣的港口設置了大型彈藥庫，儲備了約2,000噸的各式彈藥與燃油。
kitsEn: By 1941 Finnish forces had begun to modernise their weaponry. Infantry were principally equipped with the Suomi KP/31 submachine gun, the 7.62 mm Sissi M/44 carbine and the Vickers .303 machine gun. Armoured units fielded captured Soviet T‑26 and T‑28 tanks, and when needed they employed the Lahti L‑39 37 mm anti‑tank gun for point‑target elimination. Artillery comprised the 152 mm 1910/30 howitzer and the 120 mm 1938 mortar, each piece firing roughly 150 high‑explosive rounds per day. Soviet infantry divisions were equipped with Mosin‑Nagant rifles, DP‑27 light machine guns, the 45 mm 53‑K anti‑tank gun and the 122 mm 1938 howitzer. Logistics on both sides relied on a mix of trucks and horse‑drawn wagons; the Finnish rear‑area depots at Turku and ports on the Gulf of Bothnia stockpiled roughly 2,000 tons of various ammunition types and fuel.
tactics: 芬蘭在1941年的戰術以快速突破與側翼包抄為主。7月10日凌晨，芬蘭第1兵團在維堡前線集中了四個師的兵力，先以兩個152mm榴彈炮團進行為時30分鐘的密集火力準備，隨即在拂曉時分以坦克支援的第4步兵師沿著主要公路向北快速推進。同一時間，第2兵團的輕裝甲車隊繞過蘇軍第23軍團的左翼，佔領了Säkkijärvi鐵路交叉點，形成對敵側後方的威脅。蘇軍在面對突如其來的側翼攻擊時，急忙調動預備隊第7軍團的步兵團進行反衝鋒，但因缺乏有效的通訊與協調，反擊在哈爾塔師的猛烈火力下被擊退。芬蘭軍的這種「先火力後機動」戰術，在卡累利阿地峽的山地與森林地帶中發揮了極大的效果，成功在短短三週內將前線推至拉多加湖東岸。
tacticsEn: Finnish tactics in 1941 emphasised rapid breakthrough and encirclement of the flanks. In the early hours of 10 July, the Finnish I Corps massed four divisions on the Viipuri front, first unleashing a thirty‑minute intensive barrage from two 152 mm howitzer battalions, then at dawn the 4th Infantry Division, supported by tanks, advanced swiftly northward along the main highway. Simultaneously, the II Corps' light‑armoured vehicles skirted the left flank of the Soviet 23rd Army, seized the Säkkijärvi railway junction and threatened the enemy rear. Faced with this sudden flanking move, the Soviets rushed reserve infantry regiments of the 7th Army to counter‑attack, but poor communications and coordination allowed the Finnish forces, under the withering fire of Halla’s division, to repel the assault. This “fire‑then‑move” doctrine proved especially effective in the hilly, forested terrain of the Karelian Isthmus, allowing the front to be pushed to the eastern bank of Lake Ladoga within three weeks.
data: 根據芬蘭國防軍的統計，1941年7月至12月間，芬蘭軍隊在前線投入兵力約150,000人，期間有約18,000人陣亡、40,000人受傷，失蹤人數不足1,000。蘇聯紅軍在卡累利阿方向的傷亡則更為慘重，官方報告顯示約有80,000人陣亡或被俘，受傷人數估計在120,000以上。物資消耗方面，芬蘭在1941年共發射約2.5百萬發步槍彈、30萬發機槍彈以及10萬發火砲彈，燃料消耗達12,000噸。後勤列車每晝夜可向前線輸送約800噸物資，確保了前線師團的持續作戰能力。值得注意的是，蘇軍在9月的激烈戰鬥中被迫放棄了大量重型火砲，芬蘭俘獲了約30門122mm榴彈炮與15門152mm榴彈炮，進一步增強了其火力支援能力。
dataEn: According to Finnish Defence Forces statistics, between July and December 1941 the Finnish army deployed roughly 150,000 men on the front, suffering about 18,000 killed, 40,000 wounded and fewer than 1,000 missing. Soviet losses on the Karelian front were far heavier; official reports list roughly 80,000 dead or captured and an estimated 120,000 wounded. In terms of materiel, Finland expended approximately 2.5 million rifle cartridges, 300,000 machine‑gun rounds and 100,000 artillery shells in 1941, while fuel consumption reached 12,000 tons. Logistics trains delivered about 800 tons of supplies to the front each day, ensuring the sustained combat capability of the forward divisions. Notably, during September’s fierce fighting the Soviet forces were forced to abandon a large amount of heavy artillery; the Finns captured roughly 30 122 mm howitzers and 15 152 mm howitzers, further boosting their fire‑support capacity.
cause: 繼續戰爭的根本起因可追溯至1939年蘇聯對芬蘭的冬季戰爭。根據《莫斯科和平條約》，芬蘭被迫割讓卡累利阿地峽的大片領土，包括維堡，並在拉多加湖沿岸設立蘇聯軍事基地。芬蘭對此深感屈辱，並在德國於1941年6月22日發動巴巴羅薩行動後，迅速決定與納粹德國合作，以收復失土並確保國家安全。6月25日，蘇聯對芬蘭的空襲成為芬蘭正式宣戰的藉口，芬蘭政府宣稱此舉為「自衛」。此外，芬蘭高層相信，若能趁蘇聯在東線陷入苦戰之際奪回卡累利阿，將能結束長期的軍事威脅並重建國家防線。
causeEn: The root cause of the Continuation War traces back to the Winter War of 1939, when the Soviet Union forced Finland to cede large portions of the Karelian Isthmus, including Viipuri, and to allow Soviet military bases along Lake Ladoga under the Moscow Peace Treaty. The humiliation of these terms festered in Finland, and after Nazi Germany launched Operation Barbarossa on 22 June 1941, Finland quickly aligned with Germany to reclaim the lost territories and secure its national safety. The Soviet air raid on Finland on 25 June provided the formal casus belli; the Finnish government declared the action a matter of “self‑defence”. Finnish leaders believed that by taking advantage of the Soviet Union’s heavy commitments on the Eastern Front, they could recover Karelia, end the long‑standing military threat and rebuild the nation’s defensive line.
impact: 1941年的繼續戰爭對芬蘭與蘇聯的戰略格局產生了深遠影響。芬蘭在短時間內收復了包括維堡在內的卡累利阿地峽，將前線推至拉多加湖東岸，成功威脅到列寧格勒的後方供應線。蘇聯被迫從其他戰區抽調兵力防守卡累利阿，削弱了其在南方的進攻力度。此時，德國將芬蘭視為東線的重要盟友，提供武器與燃料，使得芬蘭在物資上相對充足。芬蘭的軍事勝利提升了國內的民族士氣，並在一定程度上穩定了政府的執政基礎。然而，隨著1944年蘇軍的大規模反攻，芬蘭最終被迫退出已佔領的地區，並在戰後簽署了莫斯科停戰協定，結束了這段長達三年的衝突。
impactEn: The 1941 Continuation War profoundly reshaped the strategic landscape for both Finland and the Soviet Union. Within weeks Finland reclaimed the Karelian Isthmus, including Viipuri, pushing the front to the eastern bank of Lake Ladoga and threatening the supply lines behind Leningrad. The Soviet Union had to divert forces from other fronts to defend Karelia, weakening its southern offensives. At this stage Germany treated Finland as a crucial eastern ally, supplying weapons and fuel that kept Finnish logistics comparatively healthy. The military success boosted domestic morale and reinforced the government’s authority. Nevertheless, the tables turned in 1944 when the Soviet Union launched a massive counter‑offensive, forcing Finland to abandon its occupied territories and ultimately to sign the Moscow Armistice, concluding three years of hostilities.
result: 截至1941年底，芬蘭軍隊已將控制範圍擴展至拉多加湖東岸的索爾塔瓦拉與凱姆一线，成功佔領了維堡及周邊的鐵路與公路樞紐。前線在12月初停頓於河的對岸，形成了一條長約600公里的靜止防線。芬蘭在此階段的目標基本達成：收復失土、緩解蘇聯的直接威脅，並建立了與德國的軍事合作平台。然而，蘇聯仍未放棄對芬蘭的報復行動，1942年與1943年的局部衝突顯示雙方的對抗仍在持續。直到1944年夏季，蘇軍在卡累利阿發動大規模進攻，迫使芬蘭重新談判並最終放棄了已得領土，結束了這場長期的繼續戰爭。
resultEn: By the end of 1941, Finnish forces had extended their control to the Soltavala‑Kemi line on the eastern shore of Lake Ladoga, seizing Viipuri and the surrounding railway and road junctions. The front stabilised in early December on the opposite bank of the river, creating a static line roughly 600 kilometres long. In this phase Finland had essentially achieved its objectives: recovering the lost territories, reducing the immediate Soviet threat and establishing a framework for military cooperation with Germany. Nonetheless, the Soviet Union did not abandon its designs on Finland; limited clashes in 1942 and 1943 showed that hostilities persisted. It was not until the summer of 1944 that the Soviet army launched a large‑scale offensive in Karelia, forcing Finland to renegotiate and ultimately to relinquish the conquered lands, bringing the long‑running Continuation War to a close.
